incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to government servers via an undisclosed method; internal investigation ongoing.
incidents.impact: Personal data on approximately 246,000 individuals may have been exposed; Japan's Digital Agency confirmed the breach and launched a containment review.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion via undisclosed initial access vector; exfiltrated data posted to a dark web extortion site.
incidents.impact: A limited volume of firm data was posted publicly to the dark web; Greenberg Traurig is among the largest U.S. law firms and represents high-value clients across finance, government, and tech sectors.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency wallet holders (Trezor, BitBox, CoinTracking customers)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached email marketing provider Brevo, compromising 120 client accounts and sending phishing emails from authentic company-owned domains targeting crypto holders.
incidents.impact: Thousands of hardware wallet and portfolio tracker customers received convincing phishing emails; malicious links were taken down within hours but some credential theft is expected before containment.

incidents.victim: Enterprise network operators (Cisco FMC customers — espionage cluster)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass) in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center to deploy Cyclops Blink malware, harvest firewall configurations, and pivot to managed devices.
incidents.impact: State-linked actors gained root-level access to firewall management systems, deploying a persistent implant with file transfer, credential harvesting, and network scanning capabilities; both CVEs added to CISA KEV catalog.

incidents.victim: Enterprise network operators (Cisco FMC customers — ransomware cluster)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-20316 (static credential bypass) in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center, followed by living-off-the-land lateral movement and deployment of Qilin ransomware across victim endpoints.
incidents.impact: Ransomware operators stole Active Directory credentials and domain configuration before encrypting endpoints; same vulnerability exploited in parallel by a state-sponsored espionage cluster, indicating public weaponization.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party vendor, stole API credentials, and used them to silently download patient records from Veradigm's production systems over an extended period.
incidents.impact: The Gentlemen ransomware group claims to have stolen health records for 3.5 million patients including Social Security numbers and clinical data; Veradigm confirmed a vendor API was used to exfiltrate data and notified affected health systems.

incidents.victim: Automotive and media organizations in South Korea
incidents.vector: Deployment of a new Linux espionage toolkit that embeds a persistent backdoor inside the HAProxy web proxy binary, enabling covert long-term access without alerting endpoint detection tools.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained sustained surveillance access to South Korean industrial and media targets with capabilities for remote command execution, credential harvesting, and injection of malicious content into proxied web traffic.

incidents.victim: U.S. defense contractors, aerospace firms, NGOs, and Southeast Asian government agencies
incidents.vector: At least four Chinese state-aligned groups shared a common exploit kit (BlueMoon) chaining three zero-days: two Chrome V8 RCE flaws (CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491) and a Windows ALPC privilege escalation zero-day (CVE-2026-85880), delivering full system compromise via targeted spear-phishing.
incidents.impact: Attackers implanted ShadowPad backdoors and credential-stealing browser extensions across U.S. defense contractor and aerospace networks; activity continued through at least September 8 and was still ongoing at publication; CVE-2026-87491 added to CISA KEV.

incidents.victim: IDScan (identity verification company) — 153M+ U.S. and Canadian citizens
incidents.vector: Prolonged unauthorized access to IDScan's identity verification platform — used by Hertz, Caesars Entertainment, Target, and FedEx — enabling continuous exfiltration of driver's license scans including infrared and ultraviolet images over more than one year.
incidents.impact: 153 million+ driver's license scans listed for sale on dark web marketplace 'Nexus' at approximately 400,000 new records per day; includes licenses of senior U.S. government officials (including the Defense Secretary); FBI investigating; national security implications confirmed by analysts.

incidents.attacker: Ukraine — military intelligence (HUR) and Cyber Corps
incidents.vector: Coordinated DDoS attack by Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) and affiliated hacking group Cyber Corps targeting Wildberries payment processing and order management infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Payments to marketplace sellers were disrupted; approximately 20 billion rubles (~$240 million) in seller payments remain delayed; 95% of surveyed sellers reported non-payment as of September 10.

incidents.victim: Global software supply chain — thousands of businesses via PyPI, npm, Docker Hub
incidents.vector: TeamPCP (UNC6780) embedded a self-propagating worm (Shai-Hulud) across hundreds of open-source packages on PyPI, npm, and Docker Hub; the worm harvested developer credentials and auto-propagated to additional repositories the developer had write access to.
incidents.impact: Two Australian men arrested by the Australian Federal Police on August 27; the group compromised corporate cloud environments globally and attempted to extort one victim by exfiltrating an AI code repository; infrastructure partially seized.

incidents.victim: Military and diplomatic organizations in Ukraine and Europe; North African government
incidents.vector: Russian-aligned actor used Claude AI to autonomously modify malware code to bypass detection, combined with Windows implants, mobile exploitation, browser-based credential theft, and DNS hijacking at hotel Wi-Fi vendors to reach air-gapped-adjacent targets.
incidents.impact: More than 20 government and defense organizations compromised across Ukraine and Europe; 300,000+ national identity records stolen from a North African government; a drone vision system SDK was exfiltrated; WhatsApp accounts taken over via headless browser sessions; campaign disrupted by Anthropic.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters-affiliated actors used AI to automate a software supply chain breach that exfiltrated 2,100+ Azure cloud access tokens spanning more than 40 corporate tenants in approximately 34 hours with minimal human involvement.
incidents.impact: Attackers obtained full cloud environment access for multiple corporate tenants; in a separate related breach, a single compromised developer token was escalated to full cloud environment control in approximately three hours via AI-assisted lateral movement.

incidents.victim: Anthropic and U.S. frontier AI industry (model output theft)
incidents.vector: Seven Chinese AI companies including Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Xiaomi, and Zhipu systematically harvested Claude model outputs via millions of fraudulent API requests; DeepSeek and Moonshot AI covertly proxied their own customers' queries to Claude and returned the answers as their own.
incidents.impact: Alibaba's operation alone reached nearly 3 million unauthorized exchanges per day from 3,500+ fraudulent accounts; the covert proxying exposed private user data including surveillance footage linked to a PLA-affiliated account; operations disrupted by Anthropic account terminations.
